Carcinoma arising in ovarian epithelium; reproductive organs have no axis, and ovarian origin alone does not imply endocrine disease.

Purulent infection of intraocular tissues; ancestry identifies an infectious eye disorder.
Molecular subtype of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, a malignant lymphoid-cell disease; no common additional organ damage is specified.
Chronic erosive scalp inflammation causes skin destruction and scarring alopecia; an autoimmune mechanism is not established by inflammation alone.
Bone dysplasia, skin atrophy and lipodystrophy define MAD; dental hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Enlarged globes alone do not establish eye damage.
Autoimmune polyarthritis with synovitis, erosions and progressive joint destruction; no additional organ meets the frequency threshold.
Familial glomerular hematuria associated with COL4A3; microscopic hematuria occurs in 9/9, without documented extrarenal damage.
Hereditary nephritis with renal insufficiency in 6/6 and kidney failure in 3/6; hearing impairment is documented in only 1/6, below 30%.
Pilosebaceous hamartoma involving hair follicles and epidermis, with cysts, comedones and epidermal atrophy.
Invasive carcinoma arising in bladder urothelium; the bladder belongs to the renal axis.
Defined combined immunodeficiency; no intrinsic damage to another organ is established by the supplied record.
Immune-mediated drug hypersensitivity; the umbrella does not establish lasting damage to any particular additional organ.
Cobalamin-processing defect causes methylmalonic acidemia and metabolic acidosis; lasting neurologic or renal damage is not established in >=30% of this responsive subtype.
Congenital structural abnormality of the optic disc, which belongs to the ocular axis.
Chordoma occupies the sacrum; neural compression or invasion is not established as common enough for an additional axis.
Congenital generalized hair overgrowth defines the disease; dental anomalies and deafness occur in a particular kindred, without evidence of >=30% across the condition.
Neoplasm originates in extrahepatic bile ducts, explicitly included in the hepatic axis.
Myeloid blood and marrow neoplasm encompassing therapy-related AML, MDS and related disorders; treatment causation does not change its organ of origin.
Defining ossification begins in skin and subcutis and progresses into muscle and fascia, restricting joints. Endocrine dysfunction is not intrinsic to typical POH.
Intestinal atresia and profound combined immunodeficiency define the syndrome; sparse hair and absent eyebrows do not establish functional skin damage.
Severe intellectual disability and speech delay occur in 8/8, hypotonia in 7/8 and seizures in 5/8; motor impairment reflects the neurodevelopmental disorder.
